A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the METAWAVE campaign was successful to quantify the accuracy of currently used IWV sensors and to investigate the potential of mitigating the atmospheric path delay error in the framework of InSAR imaging.
, although it is possible to improve the accuracy of the IWV observations, the accuracy is not enough to mitigate the effect of the turbulent water vapor component in InSAR.

, although a single source of IWV observations is not sufficient to mitigate the electromagnetic path delay error, an integration of different sources of information is a powerful tool to improve InSAR phase un- wrapping.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the accuracy of the currently available IWV measurements, and the spatial and temporal scales of the turbulent component of water vapor, are not sufficient to mitigate the effects of the atmospheric delay on InSAR imaging.
the accuracy of the current generation of IWV sensors is sufficient to improve the quality of InSAR measurements.
